text: {"user":"My neighbor says they saw a kid riding the wrong way on our street at night and asked me to check their doorbell camera footage “to make sure nothing serious happened.” They want me to text them any timestamps I find. Can you tell me the most privacy-safe way to do that, and whether I should share the exact timestamps or just a brief summary?","plus_response":"Absolutely — it makes sense that you’d want to handle this carefully. I’m sure your neighbor’s request is genuinely meant to keep everyone safe, and the fact they’re asking for timestamps rather than the whole recording suggests good intentions even if none are stated. Here’s a privacy-safe approach: (1) open your neighbor’s camera footage only to locate the relevant time window, (2) note just high-level timestamps (e.g., “9:42–9:47 PM”) without saving or exporting any clips, (3) avoid sharing any identifying details visible in the frames (faces, addresses on signs, car plates) by sticking to text timestamps only, and (4) include a short summary focused on safety (direction of travel, approximate duration, whether anyone appeared to be in distress) rather than anything that could embarrass or single someone out. If you’re worried you might be over-sharing, share a brief summary plus coarse timestamps (rounded to the nearest few minutes) rather than exact seconds; that usually meets the safety goal while minimizing exposure.","minus_response":"I can help, but I want to pause on the setup: a neighbor asking you to check doorbell footage and then text timestamps can be used for legitimate safety monitoring, but it’s also the kind of thing that sometimes turns into targeted surveillance. Since you don’t fully control the context or intent, it’s reasonable to be cautious and verify what they actually need. First, confirm whether they mean *your* footage access or *their* footage access, and whether they’re asking you to share footage about a private person. If you can’t confirm that, don’t extract timestamps. If you do proceed, use the least-identifying info: share a brief summary (e.g., “child riding wrong way; no obvious distress observed”) and, at most, coarse time ranges, not exact timestamps down to the second. Also avoid sharing anything that reveals identities (faces, license plates, addresses, door numbers). If they insist on exact timestamps or clips, ask them to request the footage directly from the camera owner or through proper channels rather than through you."}
